 Stan Becton | NCAA.com | November 7, 2026
 Tracking undefeated FBS college football teams in the 2026 season
 How the College Football Playoff format will work in 2026-27 
 Share 
 Going into this season, 136 teams had the opportunity to complete the perfect season. After Miami's loss to Notre Dame, TWO  undefeated teams remain: Utah and UCLA. Indiana was the last team remaining last season, running the table at 16-0 to win the CFP title. 
 Will 2026 see a team join the Hoosiers and 2023 Michigan and make it four out of the last five national champions to finish with perfect seasons?  We're tracking every undefeated team here.
 Rankings shown are the latest College Football Playoff rankings . 
 No. 3 Utah (9-0)
 Previous:  28-20 over BYU  
 Up next:   11/14 — at Arizona 
 Last undefeated season: 2008 | 13-0 | Sugar Bowl win
 Utah is the top team in the Big 12 with a resume that includes ranked wins over then-No. 18 Houston and No. 9 BYU in Week 10. The Utes will go on the road against Arizona next week carrying a nation-leading 15-game win streak. 
 No. 8 UCLA (9-0)
 Previous:   34-20 over Minnesota 
 Up next:   11/13 — vs. Illinois 
 Last undefeated season: 1954 | 9-0 | National Champions (UPI, FWAA)
 UCLA is the most surprising undefeated team left after being predicted to finish 12th in the Big Ten Preseason Poll. The Bruins have a big game still waiting in the wings, a season finale against crosstown rival Southern California.

 Stan Becton joined NCAA.com in 2021 and has since served as a college football, FCS football, track and field, cross country and HBCU beat reporter. He has covered numerous NCAA championship events, including the FCS Championship, DI Track & Field Championships and Men's Frozen Four. Additionally, he has covered the College Football Playoff and HBCU sporting events like the Celebration Bowl, MEAC/SWAC Challenge and Legacy Classic. Stan graduated from Carnegie Mellon University, earning a degree in Professional Writing and playing football as a five-year letterman. You can follow him on Twitter @stan_becton .
